_meta.indication: UKONIQ is indicated for adult patients with relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) who have received at least one prior anti-CD20-based regimen, and for adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (FL) who have received at least three prior lines of systemic therapy; both under accelerated approval based on overall response rate.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsed or refractory MZL who received 1 or more prior lines of therapy including at least 1 anti-CD20-based regimen; patients with prior PI3K inhibitor exposure excluded.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an independent review committee (IRC) based on the 2007 International Working Group criteria
pivotal_trials.result: ORR per IRC was 49% (95% CI: 37.0, 61.6), with 16% achieving complete response; median duration of response was not reached.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsed or refractory FL following at least two prior systemic therapies including an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody and an alkylating agent; approved indication restricted to those with at least three prior lines of systemic therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an independent review committee (IRC) based on modified 2007 International Working Group criteria
pivotal_trials.n: 131 patients with FL enrolled; 117 evaluable for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: ORR per IRC was 42.7% (95% CI: 33.6, 52.2), with 3.4% achieving complete response; median duration of response was 11.1 months (95% CI: 8.3, 16.4).

key_safety: Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions including lab abnormalities were increased creatinine, diarrhea-colitis, fatigue, nausea, neutropenia, transaminase elevation, musculoskeletal pain, anemia, thrombocytopenia, upper respiratory tract infection, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, and rash. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 51.2% of the safety pool, most commonly neutropenia (11.3%), diarrhea/colitis (8.4%), and increased transaminases (6.5%). Primary safety issues include serious/fatal infections and cutaneous reactions, serious diarrhea or colitis, hepatotoxicity, and neutropenia.
target_moa: Umbralisib is a small molecule inhibitor of phosphoinositide-3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) and casein kinase 1 epsilon (CK1ε); it competitively binds PI3Kδ and CK1ε, inhibiting cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis of lymphoma and leukemic cells.

rems.type: Division of Risk Management and DHM2 agreed that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of umbralisib outweigh its risks; the applicant did not submit a proposed REMS or risk management plan.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug.
